title: Packet Scanners
description: Determine the severity of passing through a firewall with periodic scanners, and compute the delay needed to avoid detection.
writeup:
## Approach

The firewall consists of layers, each containing a scanner that moves back and forth through its range. A packet moves forward one layer per picosecond. A scanner catches the packet only if it is at the top of its range at the moment the packet enters the layer.

The key observation is that each scanner moves in a predictable repeating cycle. For a scanner with range R, its position repeats every `2 * (R - 1)` picoseconds. Therefore, a packet entering depth D at time T is caught if `(T % period) == 0`.

## Part 1

The packet begins immediately, so it reaches depth D at time T = D. For each layer, we check whether the scanner is at position 0 at that time. If so, the severity for that layer is `depth * range`. Summing these values yields the total severity.

## Part 2

To avoid detection entirely, we introduce a delay before starting. With a delay of `d`, the packet reaches depth D at time `T = D + d`. We search for the smallest delay such that no layer satisfies `(D + d) % period == 0`. This brute-force search is efficient because the periodicity check is constant time.

This approach avoids simulating scanner movement and relies solely on modular arithmetic, making it both elegant and fast.
